message.content:
Create a small "pygame-like" graphical framework that can be called from COBOL programs compiled with GnuCOBOL (cobc). The framework itself may be written in any host language you think appropriate (e.g., a thin C layer over an existing cross-platform graphics/windowing library), as long as the result is a library that a COBOL program can link against and call.

The framework must let a COBOL program do the following, through whatever calling convention you design:

Initialize and later shut down the graphics subsystem.
Open a single resizable window of a requested width and height with a caller-supplied title, and obtain whatever handle(s) are needed to draw into it.
Set a current drawing color (RGBA or equivalent).
Clear the window to the current color, and present/flip the frame so drawing becomes visible.
Draw basic 2D primitives: a line between two points, an outlined rectangle, and a filled rectangle.
Poll input events in a non-blocking loop; at minimum the caller must be able to distinguish: window-close requested, a key was pressed (with which key), a key was released, mouse motion, and mouse button down/up (with which button and where).
Sleep for a given number of milliseconds, and read a monotonic millisecond tick counter.
Update the window title at runtime.
Deliver:

The framework source (C or equivalent) plus any COBOL copybook/include file needed so a COBOL program can reference event fields, key codes, and handle types symbolically rather than by magic numbers.
A build system (a Makefile is fine) that compiles the framework into a static library, then compiles a COBOL program against it into an executable.
A short README.md describing prerequisites and how to build and run.
Design notes (non-prescriptive):

You choose the function names, the way handles are represented in COBOL (pointer, opaque integer, index, ...), the event-struct layout, the argument-passing convention (BY VALUE vs BY REFERENCE), and how strings are marshalled from COBOL to C. Pick whatever makes GnuCOBOL happy and document it.
You do not need to implement text rendering, audio, or loading arbitrary image formats at this step. Plain color rectangles are enough.
You may scope to one platform (macOS, Linux, or Windows) if cross-platform is costly; just say so in the README.
Verification (required):

make (or the equivalent one-liner from your README) completes with no errors on a clean checkout.
The COBOL side compiles against your framework without needing any handwritten C glue inside the COBOL program — only a COPY of your copybook.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PYGAME-DEMO.

       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

       01 WS-RUNNING           PIC 9 VALUE 1.
       01 WS-RECT-X            BINARY-LONG VALUE 350.
       01 WS-RECT-Y            BINARY-LONG VALUE 250.
       01 WS-SPEED             BINARY-LONG VALUE 4.
       01 WS-HAS-EVENT         BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-TICKS             BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-TITLE             PIC X(80).
       01 WS-DISP-X            PIC -(4)9.
       01 WS-DISP-Y            PIC -(4)9.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PROGRAM.
           PERFORM INIT-GRAPHICS
           PERFORM GAME-LOOP UNTIL WS-RUNNING = 0
           CALL "pg_quit"
           STOP RUN.

       INIT-GRAPHICS.
           CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot initialise graphics"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           MOVE "COBOL Pygame Demo" TO WS-TITLE
           CALL "pg_open_window" USING
               BY VALUE 800
               BY VALUE 600
               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE
               BY VALUE 80
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot open window"
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.

       GAME-LOOP.
           PERFORM POLL-EVENTS
           PERFORM RENDER
           CALL "pg_delay" USING BY VALUE 16.

       POLL-EVENTS.
           CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
               RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-HAS-EVENT = 0
               EVALUATE PG-EVT-TYPE
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-QUIT
                       MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN
                       PERFORM HANDLE-KEY
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN
                       MOVE PG-EVT-MOUSE-X TO WS-RECT-X
                       MOVE PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y TO WS-RECT-Y
               END-EVALUATE
               CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
                   RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           END-PERFORM.

       HANDLE-KEY.
           EVALUATE PG-EVT-KEY
               WHEN PG-KEY-ESCAPE
                   MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
               WHEN PG-KEY-UP
                   SUBTRACT WS-SPEED FROM WS-RECT-Y
               WHEN PG-KEY-DOWN
                   ADD WS-SPEED TO WS-RECT-Y
               WHEN PG-KEY-LEFT
                   SUBTRACT WS-SPEED FROM WS-RECT-X
               WHEN PG-KEY-RIGHT
                   ADD WS-SPEED TO WS-RECT-X
               WHEN PG-KEY-W
                   SUBTRACT WS-SPEED FROM WS-RECT-Y
               WHEN PG-KEY-S
                   ADD WS-SPEED TO WS-RECT-Y
               WHEN PG-KEY-A
                   SUBTRACT WS-SPEED FROM WS-RECT-X
               WHEN PG-KEY-D
                   ADD WS-SPEED TO WS-RECT-X
           END-EVALUATE.

       RENDER.
      *>   dark-blue background
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 25 BY VALUE 25 BY VALUE 80 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_clear"

      *>   white border
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 255 BY VALUE 255 BY VALUE 255 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_draw_rect" USING
               BY VALUE 10 BY VALUE 10 BY VALUE 780 BY VALUE 580

      *>   green static rectangle
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 0 BY VALUE 180 BY VALUE 0 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_fill_rect" USING
               BY VALUE 580 BY VALUE 380 BY VALUE 140 BY VALUE 100

      *>   red player-controlled rectangle
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 220 BY VALUE 40 BY VALUE 40 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_fill_rect" USING
               BY VALUE WS-RECT-X BY VALUE WS-RECT-Y
               BY VALUE 60 BY VALUE 40

      *>   yellow diagonal line
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 255 BY VALUE 220 BY VALUE 0 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_draw_line" USING
               BY VALUE 10 BY VALUE 10 BY VALUE 790 BY VALUE 590

      *>   update window title with position
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-TICKS
           MOVE WS-RECT-X TO WS-DISP-X
           MOVE WS-RECT-Y TO WS-DISP-Y
           MOVE SPACES TO WS-TITLE
           STRING "COBOL Pygame | X:" DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  WS-DISP-X DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  " Y:" DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  WS-DISP-Y DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  INTO WS-TITLE
           END-STRING
           CALL "pg_set_title" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE
               BY VALUE 80

           CALL "pg_present".

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make          # compiles the library and the demo
./demo        # opens an 800×600 window
```

**Demo controls:**

* Arrow keys or WASD — move the red rectangle
* Left-click — teleport the red rectangle to the mouse position
* Escape or close button — quit

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `demo.cob` | Demo program (free-format COBOL) |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a` then links `demo` |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `void pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each). |
| `void pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour. |
| `void pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible. |
| `void pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points. |
| `void pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle. |
| `void pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle. |

### Input

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |

Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:

```cobol
01 PG-EVENT.
   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
```

Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `void pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The 16 ms `pg_delay` in the demo is a frame-rate safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering, audio, or image loading (colour rectangles only).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

1	# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL
2	
3	A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
4	coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
5	glue required in the COBOL source.
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	| Tool | Tested version |
10	|------|----------------|
11	| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
12	| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
13	| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
14	| GNU Make | 3.81+ |
15	
16	**macOS (Homebrew):**
17	
18	```sh
19	brew install gnucobol sdl2
20	```
21	
22	**Debian / Ubuntu:**
23	
24	```sh
25	sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
26	```
27	
28	> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
29	> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.
30	
31	## Build & run
32	
33	```sh
34	make          # compiles the library and the demo
35	./demo        # opens an 800×600 window
36	```
37	
38	**Demo controls:**
39	
40	* Arrow keys or WASD — move the red rectangle
41	* Left-click — teleport the red rectangle to the mouse position
42	* Escape or close button — quit
43	
44	`make clean` removes all build artefacts.
45	
46	## Architecture
47	
48	```
49	┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
50	│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
51	│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
52	│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
53	└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
54	```
55	
56	The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
57	never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.
58	
59	## Files
60	
61	| File | Purpose |
62	|------|---------|
63	| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
64	| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
65	| `demo.cob` | Demo program (free-format COBOL) |
66	| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a` then links `demo` |
67	
68	## API reference
69	
70	All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
71	`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
72	Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.
73	
74	### Lifecycle
75	
76	| C signature | Purpose |
77	|-------------|---------|
78	| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
79	| `void pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2. |
80	| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |
81	
82	### Drawing
83	
84	| C signature | Purpose |
85	|-------------|---------|
86	| `void pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each). |
87	| `void pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour. |
88	| `void pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible. |
89	| `void pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points. |
90	| `void pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle. |
91	| `void pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle. |
92	
93	### Input
94	
95	| C signature | Purpose |
96	|-------------|---------|
97	| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |
98	
99	Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:
100	
101	```cobol
102	01 PG-EVENT.
103	   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
104	   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
105	   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
106	   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
107	   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
108	```
109	
110	Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
111	`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.
112	
113	### Timing & misc
114	
115	| C signature | Purpose |
116	|-------------|---------|
117	| `void pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds. |
118	| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
119	| `void pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime. |
120	
121	## COBOL calling convention
122	
123	```cobol
124	WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
125	COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".
126	
127	01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
128	01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.
129	
130	PROCEDURE DIVISION.
131	    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
132	    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
133	    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
134	        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
135	        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
136	        RETURNING PG-RC
137	    ...
138	    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
139	        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
140	    ...
141	    CALL "pg_quit"
142	    STOP RUN.
143	```
144	
145	Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
146	trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.
147	
148	## Design decisions
149	
150	* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
151	  One window per process is the expected use case.
152	* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
153	  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
154	* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
155	  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
156	* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
157	  tearing.  The 16 ms `pg_delay` in the demo is a frame-rate safety net;
158	  vsync does most of the throttling.
159	* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
160	  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
161	  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).
162	
163	## Limitations
164	
165	* No text rendering, audio, or image loading (colour rectangles only).
166	* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
167	* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
168	  is untested.
169

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make          # compiles the library and the demo
./demo        # opens an 800×600 window
```

**Demo controls:**

* Arrow keys or WASD — move the red rectangle
* Left-click — teleport the red rectangle to the mouse position
* Escape or close button — quit

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `demo.cob` | Demo program (free-format COBOL) |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a` then links `demo` |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `void pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each). |
| `void pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour. |
| `void pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible. |
| `void pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points. |
| `void pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle. |
| `void pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle. |

### Input

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |

Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:

```cobol
01 PG-EVENT.
   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
```

Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `void pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The 16 ms `pg_delay` in the demo is a frame-rate safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering, audio, or image loading (colour rectangles only).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

       01 WS-BOX-H             BINARY-LONG VALUE 48.

       01 WS-FRAME-END         BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-ELAPSED           BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-SLEEP-MS          BINARY-LONG.

      *> scratch
       01 WS-EDGE              BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-TITLE             PIC X(80).

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PROGRAM.
           PERFORM INIT-GRAPHICS
           PERFORM GAME-LOOP UNTIL WS-RUNNING = 0
           CALL "pg_quit"
           STOP RUN.

       INIT-GRAPHICS.
           CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot initialise graphics"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           MOVE "COBOL Bouncing Box" TO WS-TITLE
           CALL "pg_open_window" USING
               BY VALUE 640
               BY VALUE 480
               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE
               BY VALUE 80
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot open window"
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.

       GAME-LOOP.
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-START
           PERFORM POLL-EVENTS
           PERFORM UPDATE-STATE
           PERFORM RENDER
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-END
           COMPUTE WS-ELAPSED = WS-FRAME-END - WS-FRAME-START
           IF WS-ELAPSED < 16
               COMPUTE WS-SLEEP-MS = 16 - WS-ELAPSED
               CALL "pg_delay" USING BY VALUE WS-SLEEP-MS
           END-IF.

       POLL-EVENTS.
           CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
               RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-HAS-EVENT = 0
               EVALUATE PG-EVT-TYPE
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-QUIT
                       MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN
                       IF PG-EVT-KEY = PG-KEY-ESCAPE
                           MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                       END-IF
               END-EVALUATE
               CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
                   RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           END-PERFORM.

           ADD WS-VX TO WS-BOX-X
           ADD WS-VY TO WS-BOX-Y

      *>   bounce horizontally
           IF WS-BOX-X < 0

               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-BOX-X + WS-BOX-W
               IF WS-EDGE > 640
                   COMPUTE WS-BOX-X = 640 - WS-BOX-W
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
               END-IF
           END-IF

      *>   bounce vertically
           IF WS-BOX-Y < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-BOX-Y
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-BOX-Y + WS-BOX-H
               IF WS-EDGE > 480
                   COMPUTE WS-BOX-Y = 480 - WS-BOX-H
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
               END-IF

      *>   dark background
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING

               BY VALUE WS-BOX-X BY VALUE WS-BOX-Y

           CALL "pg_draw_rect" USING
               BY VALUE WS-BOX-X BY VALUE WS-BOX-Y
               BY VALUE WS-BOX-W BY VALUE WS-BOX-H

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make          # compiles the library and the demo
./demo        # opens an 800×600 window
```

**Demo controls:**

* Arrow keys or WASD — move the red rectangle
* Left-click — teleport the red rectangle to the mouse position
* Escape or close button — quit

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `demo.cob` | Demo program (free-format COBOL) |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a` then links `demo` |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `void pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make          # compiles the library, demo, and bounce
make run      # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
./demo        # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
./bounce      # animated bouncing box (no input required)
```

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

### bounce (animated example)

Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
window's close button to exit cleanly.

### demo (interactive example)

Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## GnuCOBOL static-call fix

By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
executable, the runtime will fail with:

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

The fix is the **`-fstatic-call`** compiler flag, which makes `cobc`
generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
Makefile already passes this flag:

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

`COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
-  tearing.  The 16 ms `pg_delay` in the demo is a frame-rate safety net;
+  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).

Clean build, zero warnings, all three artefacts produced. Here's what was done:

**New file: `bounce.cob`** — a self-contained bouncing-box demo that:
- Opens a 640x480 window titled "COBOL Bouncing Box"
- Animates a cyan filled rectangle (with white outline) bouncing off all four edges
- Uses measure-and-sleep timing: reads `pg_get_ticks` before and after each frame, sleeps only the remaining time to hit 16 ms (~60 fps)
- Exits cleanly on Escape or window-close (calls `pg_quit`, then `STOP RUN`)
- Contains only COBOL + `COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy"` — no C glue

**Updated `Makefile`:**
- `make` builds both `demo` and `bounce`
- `make run` builds and launches `bounce`
- Shared `COB_FLAGS` variable includes `-fstatic-call`

**Updated `README.md`:**
- New "GnuCOBOL static-call fix" section explaining the `dlsym` pitfall and the `-fstatic-call` solution
- Documents both examples and `make run`

Run `make run` (or `./bounce`) to see the animation.

Extend the framework from Step 1 so that a COBOL program can load an image from disk and draw it into the window.

Requirements:

Support at least one common image file format that can be loaded without pulling in a heavyweight third-party dependency (e.g., BMP is a reasonable minimum; if the underlying library you chose already supports more, expose more).
A COBOL program can: load an image from a file path into an opaque texture/surface handle, learn its pixel dimensions, draw it at an (x, y) position with an optional destination size, and later release the handle.
Errors (file missing, unsupported format, out of memory, etc.) are reported in a way a COBOL program can detect and surface — for example a non-zero return code plus a way to retrieve a human-readable error string into a COBOL buffer.
Update the copybook (or equivalent) so the COBOL side has names for the new handle type and any new constants.

Verification (required):

Add a tiny test program or extend the Step 2 example so that pressing a key (or just at startup) loads a small image you ship in the repo and draws it. The image must appear in the window.
Deliberately loading a missing file returns a detectable error to the COBOL caller and does not crash.

CC         = cc
COBC       = cobc
AR         = ar

SDL_CFLAGS = $(shell sdl2-config --cflags)
SDL_LIBS   = $(shell sdl2-config --libs)
COB_FLAGS  = -x -free -fstatic-call

.PHONY: all clean run

all: demo bounce

# ── framework static library ──────────────────────────────
pygame_cobol.o: pygame_cobol.c
	$(CC) -c -Wall -O2 $(SDL_CFLAGS) -o $@ $<

libpygame_cobol.a: pygame_cobol.o
	$(AR) rcs $@ $<

           CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC

           CALL "pg_open_window" USING

               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE

               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot open window"
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.

       TEST-ERROR-HANDLING.
           DISPLAY "--- Testing error handling ---"
           MOVE "nonexistent.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC = -1
               DISPLAY "  Load correctly failed (rc=-1)"
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "  Error: " PG-ERROR-MSG

           END-IF
           DISPLAY "--- Error handling OK ---".

           MOVE "test.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING WS-IMG-HANDLE
           IF WS-IMG-HANDLE = -1
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "Cannot load test.bmp: " PG-ERROR-MSG
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           PERFORM POLL-EVENTS
           PERFORM UPDATE-STATE

           COMPUTE WS-ELAPSED = WS-FRAME-END - WS-FRAME-START
           IF WS-ELAPSED < 16

                       END-IF
               END-EVALUATE

           END-PERFORM.

           ADD WS-VY TO WS-IMG-Y

                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
               END-IF
           END-IF.

           CALL "pg_draw_image_sized" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 96
               BY VALUE 96

           CALL "pg_present".

	./imgtest

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make          # compiles the library, demo, and bounce
make run      # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
./demo        # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
./bounce      # animated bouncing box (no input required)
```

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

### bounce (animated example)

Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
window's close button to exit cleanly.

### demo (interactive example)

Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `bounce.cob` | Animated bouncing-box example (free-format COBOL) |
| `demo.cob` | Interactive demo — keyboard & mouse (free-format COBOL) |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a` then links both examples |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `void pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each). |
| `void pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour. |
| `void pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible. |
| `void pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points. |
| `void pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle. |
| `void pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle. |

### Input

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |

Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:

```cobol
01 PG-EVENT.
   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
```

Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `void pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## GnuCOBOL static-call fix

By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
executable, the runtime will fail with:

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

The fix is the **`-fstatic-call`** compiler flag, which makes `cobc`
generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
Makefile already passes this flag:

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering, audio, or image loading (colour rectangles only).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make              # compiles the library, all examples, and test.bmp
make run          # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
make run-imgtest  # builds and launches the image-loading test
./demo            # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
./bounce          # animated bouncing box (no input required)
./imgtest         # image loading, error handling, and drawing
```

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

### bounce (animated example)

Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
window's close button to exit cleanly.

### imgtest (image loading test)

On startup: deliberately tries to load a missing file and prints the
error to the terminal (verifies error detection).  Then loads the
shipped `test.bmp`, queries its dimensions, and bounces it around the
window at native size while also drawing a 2× scaled copy in the
top-left corner.

### demo (interactive example)

Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `bounce.cob` | Animated bouncing-box example (free-format COBOL) |
| `demo.cob` | Interactive demo — keyboard & mouse (free-format COBOL) |
| `imgtest.cob` | Image loading & error-handling test (free-format COBOL) |
| `gen_test_bmp.c` | Generates `test.bmp` (48×48 24-bit BMP) at build time |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a`, generates `test.bmp`, links all examples |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `void pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each). |
| `void pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour. |
| `void pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible. |
| `void pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points. |
| `void pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle. |
| `void pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle. |

### Input

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |

Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:

```cobol
01 PG-EVENT.
   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
```

Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `void pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## GnuCOBOL static-call fix

By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
executable, the runtime will fail with:

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

The fix is the **`-fstatic-call`** compiler flag, which makes `cobc`
generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
Makefile already passes this flag:

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering, audio, or image loading (colour rectangles only).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

content.text:
Everything builds with zero warnings. Here's a summary of what was added:

### Framework extension (`pygame_cobol.c`)

**7 new functions:**
- `pg_load_image(path, path_len)` — loads a BMP via `SDL_LoadBMP`, converts to texture, returns a 1-based integer handle (or -1 on error)
- `pg_image_width(handle)` / `pg_image_height(handle)` — query pixel dimensions
- `pg_draw_image(handle, x, y)` — draw at native size
- `pg_draw_image_sized(handle, x, y, w, h)` — draw scaled
- `pg_free_image(handle)` — release texture
- `pg_get_error(buf, buf_len)` — copy last error string into a COBOL buffer (space-padded)

Textures are stored in a 64-slot table indexed by handle. `pg_quit` frees all remaining textures.

### Copybook (`pygame_cobol.cpy`)
Added `PG-ERROR-MSG PIC X(256)` for `pg_get_error` output.

### New files
- **`gen_test_bmp.c`** — generates a 48×48 BMP (red cross on blue field with white border)
- **`imgtest.cob`** — test program that:
  1. Attempts to load `nonexistent.bmp` → prints the error (verifies error path)
  2. Loads `test.bmp`, prints its dimensions
  3. Bounces the image around the window + draws a 2× scaled copy in the corner

### Makefile
Added `imgtest`, `gen_test_bmp`, `test.bmp` targets and `make run-imgtest`.

Run `make run-imgtest` to see the image bouncing in the window and the error-handling output on the terminal.

           MOVE "nonexistent.bmp" TO WS-PATH

               RETURNING PG-RC

Builds clean. Please run `make run-imgtest` — the debug output will show whether `WS-RUNNING` is still `1` before the loop and whether the loop body executes at all. This will tell us exactly where the problem is.

The key change: every `void` function in `pygame_cobol.c` now returns `int` (always 0). GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` declares all externals as `extern int name()`, so calling a `void` function through that declaration was undefined behavior — the caller read garbage from the return register. This may have been corrupting GnuCOBOL's `RETURN-CODE` in a way that interfered with program flow.

```cobol

    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user requested a multi-step project to create a "pygame-like" graphical framework callable from GnuCOBOL programs:
   - **Step 1**: Create the core framework (C/SDL2 wrapper) with init/quit, window management, RGBA colors, drawing primitives (line, rect, fill_rect), event polling (quit, key, mouse), timing (delay, ticks), title updates. Plus a COBOL copybook, Makefile, and README.
   - **Step 2**: Write an animated bouncing rectangle demo (`bounce.cob`) proving the framework works end-to-end at ~60fps with clean exit.
   - **Step 3**: Extend the framework with image loading (BMP minimum), including load/query dimensions/draw/draw-scaled/free/error-reporting functions. Ship a test image and a test program that verifies both successful loading and error handling for missing files.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 (`cobc`) compiling free-format COBOL with `-fstatic-call` flag
   - SDL2 2.32.x as the graphics backend (built-in `SDL_LoadBMP` for BMP support, no extra deps)
   - Singleton window/renderer pattern (COBOL never handles pointers)
   - COBOL-to-C interop: `CALL "func" USING BY VALUE / BY REFERENCE ... RETURNING var`
   - BINARY-LONG maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding
   - COBOL strings are space-padded PIC X(n), C side trims trailing spaces
   - GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` flag generates direct C function calls instead of runtime dlsym lookups
   - GnuCOBOL generates `extern int funcname()` (K&R style) for ALL external functions, even void ones
   - Level 78 constants in COBOL copybooks for symbolic event types and key codes
   - Texture handle table: 1-based integer handles into a fixed 64-slot array
   - `pg_get_error` copies last error into COBOL buffer with space-padding
   - Measure-and-sleep timing pattern for ~60fps

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **`pygame_cobol.c`** - Core framework implementation (C/SDL2 wrapper)
     - Contains 20 functions: pg_init, pg_quit, pg_open_window, pg_set_color, pg_clear, pg_present, pg_draw_line, pg_draw_rect, pg_fill_rect, pg_poll_event, pg_delay, pg_get_ticks, pg_set_title, pg_load_image, pg_image_width, pg_image_height, pg_draw_image, pg_draw_image_sized, pg_free_image, pg_get_error
     - Singleton g_window/g_renderer plus g_textures[64] slot table and g_last_error[256]
     - `cobol_to_cstr()` helper trims COBOL space-padded strings
     - `pg_load_image` probes with `fopen` before `SDL_LoadBMP` for better error messages
     - `pg_get_error` space-fills the COBOL buffer after copying the error string
     - `pg_quit` frees all loaded textures before destroying renderer/window
     - **CRITICAL ISSUE**: Many functions (pg_quit, pg_set_color, pg_clear, pg_present, pg_draw_line, pg_draw_rect, pg_fill_rect, pg_delay, pg_free_image, pg_get_error, pg_draw_image, pg_draw_image_sized) return `void` but GnuCOBOL declares them all as `extern int funcname()`. This causes undefined behavior when GnuCOBOL reads the garbage return value.
     - Key function signatures:
       ```c
       int pg_load_image(const char *path, int path_len);  // returns handle (1-64) or -1
       int pg_image_width(int handle);   // returns width or 0
       int pg_image_height(int handle);  // returns height or 0
       void pg_draw_image(int handle, int x, int y);
       void pg_draw_image_sized(int handle, int x, int y, int w, int h);
       void pg_free_image(int handle);
       void pg_get_error(char *buf, int buf_len);  // space-pads COBOL buffer
       ```

   - **`pygame_cobol.cpy`** - COBOL copybook
     - 78-level constants for event types (PG-EVENT-NONE through PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP, values 0-6)
     - 78-level constants for key codes (ASCII values for letters, SDL extended codes for arrows/F-keys)
     - 78-level constants for mouse buttons (LEFT=1, MIDDLE=2, RIGHT=3)
     - PG-EVENT group record (5 BINARY-LONG fields = 20 bytes matching C struct pg_event_t)

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. IMAGE-TEST.

       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

       01 WS-RUNNING           PIC 9 VALUE 1.
       01 WS-HAS-EVENT         BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-TITLE             PIC X(80).
       01 WS-PATH              PIC X(256).

      *> image handle and dimensions
       01 WS-IMG-HANDLE        BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-IMG-W             BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-IMG-H             BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.

      *> bouncing image position
       01 WS-IMG-X             BINARY-LONG VALUE 100.
       01 WS-IMG-Y             BINARY-LONG VALUE 80.
       01 WS-VX                BINARY-LONG VALUE 2.
       01 WS-VY                BINARY-LONG VALUE 3.

      *> timing
       01 WS-FRAME-START       BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-FRAME-END         BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-ELAPSED           BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-SLEEP-MS          BINARY-LONG.

      *> scratch
       01 WS-EDGE              BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-DISP-W            PIC Z(4)9.
       01 WS-DISP-H            PIC Z(4)9.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PROGRAM.
           PERFORM INIT-GRAPHICS
           PERFORM TEST-ERROR-HANDLING
           PERFORM LOAD-TEST-IMAGE
           PERFORM GAME-LOOP UNTIL WS-RUNNING = 0
           CALL "pg_free_image" USING BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
           CALL "pg_quit"
           STOP RUN.

       INIT-GRAPHICS.
           CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot initialise graphics"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           MOVE "COBOL Image Test" TO WS-TITLE
           CALL "pg_open_window" USING
               BY VALUE 640
               BY VALUE 480
               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE
               BY VALUE 80
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot open window"
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.

       TEST-ERROR-HANDLING.
           DISPLAY "--- Testing error handling ---"
           MOVE "nonexistent.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC = -1
               DISPLAY "  Load correctly failed (rc=-1)"
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "  Error: " PG-ERROR-MSG
           ELSE
               DISPLAY "  BUG: load should have failed!"
           END-IF
           DISPLAY "--- Error handling OK ---".

       LOAD-TEST-IMAGE.
           MOVE "test.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING WS-IMG-HANDLE
           IF WS-IMG-HANDLE = -1
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "Cannot load test.bmp: " PG-ERROR-MSG
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           CALL "pg_image_width" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               RETURNING WS-IMG-W
           CALL "pg_image_height" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               RETURNING WS-IMG-H
           MOVE WS-IMG-W TO WS-DISP-W
           MOVE WS-IMG-H TO WS-DISP-H
           DISPLAY "Loaded test.bmp: "
                   FUNCTION TRIM(WS-DISP-W) "x"
                   FUNCTION TRIM(WS-DISP-H) " pixels".

       GAME-LOOP.
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-START
           PERFORM POLL-EVENTS
           PERFORM UPDATE-STATE
           PERFORM RENDER
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-END
           COMPUTE WS-ELAPSED = WS-FRAME-END - WS-FRAME-START
           IF WS-ELAPSED < 16
               COMPUTE WS-SLEEP-MS = 16 - WS-ELAPSED
               CALL "pg_delay" USING BY VALUE WS-SLEEP-MS
           END-IF.

       POLL-EVENTS.
           CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
               RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-HAS-EVENT = 0
               EVALUATE PG-EVT-TYPE
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-QUIT
                       MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN
                       IF PG-EVT-KEY = PG-KEY-ESCAPE
                           MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                       END-IF
               END-EVALUATE
               CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
                   RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           END-PERFORM.

       UPDATE-STATE.
           ADD WS-VX TO WS-IMG-X
           ADD WS-VY TO WS-IMG-Y

      *>   bounce horizontally
           IF WS-IMG-X < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-IMG-X
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-IMG-X + WS-IMG-W
               IF WS-EDGE > 640
                   COMPUTE WS-IMG-X = 640 - WS-IMG-W
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
               END-IF
           END-IF

      *>   bounce vertically
           IF WS-IMG-Y < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-IMG-Y
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-IMG-Y + WS-IMG-H
               IF WS-EDGE > 480
                   COMPUTE WS-IMG-Y = 480 - WS-IMG-H
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
               END-IF
           END-IF.

       RENDER.
      *>   dark background
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 30 BY VALUE 30 BY VALUE 50 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_clear"

      *>   bouncing image at native size
           CALL "pg_draw_image" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-X
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-Y

      *>   scaled copy (2x) pinned in the top-left corner
           CALL "pg_draw_image_sized" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 96
               BY VALUE 96

           CALL "pg_present".

CC         = cc
COBC       = cobc
AR         = ar

SDL_CFLAGS = $(shell sdl2-config --cflags)
SDL_LIBS   = $(shell sdl2-config --libs)
COB_FLAGS  = -x -free -fstatic-call

.PHONY: all clean run run-imgtest

all: demo bounce imgtest

# ── framework static library ──────────────────────────────
pygame_cobol.o: pygame_cobol.c
	$(CC) -c -Wall -O2 $(SDL_CFLAGS) -o $@ $<

libpygame_cobol.a: pygame_cobol.o
	$(AR) rcs $@ $<

# ── test image ────────────────────────────────────────────
gen_test_bmp: gen_test_bmp.c
	$(CC) -Wall -O2 -o $@ $<

test.bmp: gen_test_bmp
	./gen_test_bmp

# ── COBOL programs ────────────────────────────────────────
demo: demo.cob libpygame_cobol.a pygame_cobol.cpy
	$(COBC) $(COB_FLAGS) demo.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(SDL_LIBS)

bounce: bounce.cob libpygame_cobol.a pygame_cobol.cpy
	$(COBC) $(COB_FLAGS) bounce.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(SDL_LIBS)

imgtest: imgtest.cob libpygame_cobol.a pygame_cobol.cpy test.bmp
	$(COBC) $(COB_FLAGS) imgtest.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(SDL_LIBS)

run: bounce
	./bounce

run-imgtest: imgtest
	./imgtest

clean:
	rm -f *.o *.a demo bounce imgtest gen_test_bmp test.bmp

* **All C functions return `int`** — GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits

1	# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL
2	
3	A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
4	coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
5	glue required in the COBOL source.
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	| Tool | Tested version |
10	|------|----------------|
11	| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
12	| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
13	| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
14	| GNU Make | 3.81+ |
15	
16	**macOS (Homebrew):**
17	
18	```sh
19	brew install gnucobol sdl2
20	```
21	
22	**Debian / Ubuntu:**
23	
24	```sh
25	sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
26	```
27	
28	> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
29	> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.
30	
31	## Build & run
32	
33	```sh
34	make              # compiles the library, all examples, and test.bmp
35	make run          # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
36	make run-imgtest  # builds and launches the image-loading test
37	./demo            # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
38	./bounce          # animated bouncing box (no input required)
39	./imgtest         # image loading, error handling, and drawing
40	```
41	
42	`make clean` removes all build artefacts.
43	
44	### bounce (animated example)
45	
46	Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
47	~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
48	window's close button to exit cleanly.
49	
50	### imgtest (image loading test)
51	
52	On startup: deliberately tries to load a missing file and prints the
53	error to the terminal (verifies error detection).  Then loads the
54	shipped `test.bmp`, queries its dimensions, and bounces it around the
55	window at native size while also drawing a 2× scaled copy in the
56	top-left corner.
57	
58	### demo (interactive example)
59	
60	Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
61	left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.
62	
63	## Architecture
64	
65	```
66	┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
67	│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
68	│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
69	│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
70	└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
71	```
72	
73	The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
74	never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.
75	
76	## Files
77	
78	| File | Purpose |
79	|------|---------|
80	| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
81	| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
82	| `bounce.cob` | Animated bouncing-box example (free-format COBOL) |
83	| `demo.cob` | Interactive demo — keyboard & mouse (free-format COBOL) |
