# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make              # compiles the library, all examples, and test.bmp
make run          # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
make run-imgtest  # builds and launches the image-loading test
./demo            # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
./bounce          # animated bouncing box (no input required)
./imgtest         # image loading, error handling, and drawing
```

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

### bounce (animated example)

Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
window's close button to exit cleanly.

### imgtest (image loading test)

On startup: deliberately tries to load a missing file and prints the
error to the terminal (verifies error detection).  Then loads the
shipped `test.bmp`, queries its dimensions, and bounces it around the
window at native size while also drawing a 2× scaled copy in the
top-left corner.

### demo (interactive example)

Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `bounce.cob` | Animated bouncing-box example (free-format COBOL) |
| `demo.cob` | Interactive demo — keyboard & mouse (free-format COBOL) |
| `imgtest.cob` | Image loading & error-handling test (free-format COBOL) |
| `gen_test_bmp.c` | Generates `test.bmp` (48×48 24-bit BMP) at build time |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a`, generates `test.bmp`, links all examples |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `void pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each). |
| `void pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour. |
| `void pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible. |
| `void pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points. |
| `void pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle. |
| `void pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle. |

### Input

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |

Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:

```cobol
01 PG-EVENT.
   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
```

Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.

### Images

Supports **BMP** files (SDL2's built-in loader — no extra dependency).
Handles are 1-based integers (BINARY-LONG); -1 means error.

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_load_image(path, path_len)` | Load a BMP file.  Returns a handle (≥ 1) or -1 on error. |
| `int pg_image_width(int handle)` | Pixel width of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `int pg_image_height(int handle)` | Pixel height of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `void pg_draw_image(int handle, int x, int y)` | Draw the image at (x, y) at its native size. |
| `void pg_draw_image_sized(int handle, int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw the image scaled to w × h. |
| `void pg_free_image(int handle)` | Release the texture.  Safe to call twice. |
| `void pg_get_error(char *buf, int buf_len)` | Copy the last error message into a COBOL buffer (space-padded). |

Up to 64 images may be loaded simultaneously.

Example (COBOL):

```cobol
01 WS-PATH   PIC X(256).
01 WS-HANDLE BINARY-LONG.

MOVE "sprite.bmp" TO WS-PATH
CALL "pg_load_image" USING
    BY REFERENCE WS-PATH BY VALUE 256
    RETURNING WS-HANDLE
IF WS-HANDLE = -1
    CALL "pg_get_error" USING
        BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG BY VALUE 256
    DISPLAY "Load failed: " PG-ERROR-MSG
END-IF
```

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `void pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## GnuCOBOL static-call fix

By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
executable, the runtime will fail with:

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

The fix is the **`-fstatic-call`** compiler flag, which makes `cobc`
generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
Makefile already passes this flag:

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |

**Debian / Ubuntu:**


> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make              # compiles the library, all examples, and test.bmp
make run          # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
make run-imgtest  # builds and launches the image-loading test
./demo            # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
./bounce          # animated bouncing box (no input required)
./imgtest         # image loading, error handling, and drawing
```

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

### bounce (animated example)

Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
window's close button to exit cleanly.

### imgtest (image loading test)

On startup: deliberately tries to load a missing file and prints the
error to the terminal (verifies error detection).  Then loads the
shipped `test.bmp`, queries its dimensions, and bounces it around the
window at native size while also drawing a 2× scaled copy in the

### demo (interactive example)

Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐

│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
```

never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |

| C signature | Purpose |

```cobol
IF WS-HANDLE = -1

        BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG BY VALUE 256
    DISPLAY "Load failed: " PG-ERROR-MSG
END-IF
```

Supports **BMP** files (SDL2's built-in loader — no extra dependency).
Handles are 1-based integers (BINARY-LONG); -1 means error.

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_load_image(path, path_len)` | Load a BMP file.  Returns a handle (≥ 1) or -1 on error. |
| `int pg_image_width(int handle)` | Pixel width of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `int pg_image_height(int handle)` | Pixel height of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `int pg_draw_image(int handle, int x, int y)` | Draw the image at (x, y) at its native size.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_draw_image_sized(int handle, int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw the image scaled to w × h.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_free_image(int handle)` | Release the texture.  Safe to call twice.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_get_error(char *buf, int buf_len)` | Copy the last error message into a COBOL buffer (space-padded).  Returns 0. |

Up to 64 images may be loaded simultaneously.

Example (COBOL):

```cobol
01 WS-PATH   PIC X(256).
01 WS-HANDLE BINARY-LONG.

MOVE "sprite.bmp" TO WS-PATH
CALL "pg_load_image" USING
    BY REFERENCE WS-PATH BY VALUE 256
    RETURNING WS-HANDLE
IF WS-HANDLE = -1
    CALL "pg_get_error" USING
        BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG BY VALUE 256
    DISPLAY "Load failed: " PG-ERROR-MSG
END-IF
```

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `void pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `void pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## GnuCOBOL static-call fix

By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
executable, the runtime will fail with:

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

The fix is the **`-fstatic-call`** compiler flag, which makes `cobc`
generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
Makefile already passes this flag:

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **All C functions return `int`** — GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits
  `extern int name()` (K&R style) for every external `CALL`.  If the
  actual C function returns `void`, the caller reads garbage from the
  return register, which is undefined behaviour.  On ARM64 this can
  silently corrupt GnuCOBOL's `RETURN-CODE` and break control flow.
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

content.text:
The bug is fixed. The root cause: GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` declares every external function as `extern int name()`. Our `void` functions didn't set the return register, so GnuCOBOL read garbage into `RETURN-CODE` after each call. On ARM64, this undefined behavior silently broke program flow — the loop condition or a `STOP RUN` path was triggered by the garbage value.

The fix: all 13 formerly-`void` functions in `pygame_cobol.c` now return `int` (always 0), matching what GnuCOBOL expects. The README is updated with the new signatures and a design note about this pitfall.

The root cause: `FUNCTION TRIM` (`cob_intr_trim`) inside a PERFORMed paragraph corrupts GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 runtime state on ARM64, causing the subsequent `PERFORM UNTIL` to skip. Fix: move the TRIM display into MAIN-PROGRAM where the `cob_display` call itself serves as the state-restoring function call before the loop.

       COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

       01 WS-RUNNING           BINARY-LONG VALUE 1.
       01 WS-HAS-EVENT         BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-TITLE             PIC X(80).
       01 WS-PATH              PIC X(256).

      *> image handle and dimensions
       01 WS-IMG-HANDLE        BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-IMG-W             BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-IMG-H             BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.

      *> bouncing image position
       01 WS-IMG-X             BINARY-LONG VALUE 100.
       01 WS-IMG-Y             BINARY-LONG VALUE 80.
       01 WS-VX                BINARY-LONG VALUE 2.
       01 WS-VY                BINARY-LONG VALUE 3.

      *> timing
       01 WS-FRAME-START       BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-FRAME-END         BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-ELAPSED           BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-SLEEP-MS          BINARY-LONG.

      *> scratch
       01 WS-EDGE              BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-DISP-W            PIC Z(4)9.
       01 WS-DISP-H            PIC Z(4)9.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PROGRAM.
           PERFORM INIT-GRAPHICS
           PERFORM TEST-ERROR-HANDLING
           PERFORM LOAD-TEST-IMAGE
           PERFORM GAME-LOOP UNTIL WS-RUNNING = 0
           CALL "pg_free_image" USING BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
           CALL "pg_quit"
           STOP RUN.

       INIT-GRAPHICS.
           CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot initialise graphics"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           MOVE "COBOL Image Test" TO WS-TITLE
           CALL "pg_open_window" USING
               BY VALUE 640
               BY VALUE 480
               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE
               BY VALUE 80
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot open window"
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.

       TEST-ERROR-HANDLING.
           DISPLAY "--- Testing error handling ---"
           MOVE "nonexistent.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC = -1
               DISPLAY "  Load correctly failed (rc=-1)"
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "  Error: " PG-ERROR-MSG
           ELSE
               DISPLAY "  BUG: load should have failed!"
           END-IF
           DISPLAY "--- Error handling OK ---".

       LOAD-TEST-IMAGE.
           MOVE "test.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING WS-IMG-HANDLE
           IF WS-IMG-HANDLE = -1
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "Cannot load test.bmp: " PG-ERROR-MSG
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           CALL "pg_image_width" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               RETURNING WS-IMG-W
           CALL "pg_image_height" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               RETURNING WS-IMG-H
           MOVE WS-IMG-W TO WS-DISP-W
           MOVE WS-IMG-H TO WS-DISP-H
           DISPLAY "Loaded test.bmp: "
                   WS-IMG-W "x" WS-IMG-H " pixels".

       GAME-LOOP.
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-START
           PERFORM POLL-EVENTS
           PERFORM UPDATE-STATE
           PERFORM RENDER
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-END
           COMPUTE WS-ELAPSED = WS-FRAME-END - WS-FRAME-START
           IF WS-ELAPSED < 16
               COMPUTE WS-SLEEP-MS = 16 - WS-ELAPSED
               CALL "pg_delay" USING BY VALUE WS-SLEEP-MS
           END-IF.

       POLL-EVENTS.
           CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
               RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-HAS-EVENT = 0
               EVALUATE PG-EVT-TYPE
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-QUIT
                       MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN
                       IF PG-EVT-KEY = PG-KEY-ESCAPE
                           MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                       END-IF
               END-EVALUATE
               CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
                   RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           END-PERFORM.

       UPDATE-STATE.
           ADD WS-VX TO WS-IMG-X
           ADD WS-VY TO WS-IMG-Y

      *>   bounce horizontally
           IF WS-IMG-X < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-IMG-X
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-IMG-X + WS-IMG-W
               IF WS-EDGE > 640
                   COMPUTE WS-IMG-X = 640 - WS-IMG-W
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
               END-IF
           END-IF

      *>   bounce vertically
           IF WS-IMG-Y < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-IMG-Y
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-IMG-Y + WS-IMG-H
               IF WS-EDGE > 480
                   COMPUTE WS-IMG-Y = 480 - WS-IMG-H
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
               END-IF
           END-IF.

       RENDER.
      *>   dark background
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 30 BY VALUE 30 BY VALUE 50 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_clear"

      *>   bouncing image at native size
           CALL "pg_draw_image" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-X
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-Y

      *>   scaled copy (2x) pinned in the top-left corner
           CALL "pg_draw_image_sized" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 96
               BY VALUE 96

           CALL "pg_present".

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

Thin C/SDL2 wrapper (libpygame_cobol.a) providing window management,
drawing primitives, event polling, timing, and BMP image loading —
all callable from free-format COBOL via CALL "pg_*" with -fstatic-call.

Includes three demo programs: interactive demo (demo.cob), bouncing
box animation (bounce.cob), and image loading test (imgtest.cob).

All C functions return int (not void) because GnuCOBOL's -fstatic-call
emits 'extern int name()' for every external symbol — void returns
cause undefined behaviour on ARM64. FUNCTION TRIM is avoided inside
PERFORMed paragraphs due to a GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 cob_intr_trim bug on
ARM64/macOS that corrupts runtime state and breaks PERFORM UNTIL loops.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

message.content:
Using the framework from Steps 1–3, implement Flappy Bird as a COBOL program. No C code inside the game itself — game logic, physics, rendering calls, input handling, and scoring all live in a single .cob file that uses the framework.

Behavior:

A tall portrait-ish window (roughly 480 x 640 works well, but you pick).
A "bird" (a single colored rectangle is fine) sits at a fixed horizontal position. Gravity pulls it downward each frame. Pressing Space, Up-arrow, or clicking the left mouse button applies an upward impulse ("flap").
A small number of "pipes" (3 is enough) scroll from right to left at a constant speed. Each pipe has a vertical gap the bird must fly through. When a pipe exits the left edge, it wraps around to the right with a newly randomized gap position.
There is a ground strip at the bottom that the bird can crash into.
Collision detection: if the bird's bounding box overlaps any pipe (top or bottom segment) or touches the ground, the game enters a "game over" state.
Score: each time the bird successfully passes a pipe, score increments by 1. The score is visible to the player — displaying it in the window title is fine (text rendering inside the window is not required).
Game-over state: the bird stops moving, input no longer flaps; pressing Space (or clicking) resets the game to its initial state with score 0.
The main loop is frame-rate-limited to roughly 60 FPS.
Escape or the window-close button exits cleanly.
Wire the game into the build system so it builds alongside the Step 2 example and can be run with a single command (e.g., make run-flappy).

Verification (required):

Building the whole project from a clean state succeeds with one make invocation.
Running the game: a window appears with sky/pipes/ground/bird visible; gravity pulls the bird down if nothing is pressed; pressing Space flaps the bird up; pipes scroll leftward; flying into a pipe or the ground ends the game; pressing Space after a game-over restarts it; the score visibly increments when a pipe is passed; Escape exits cleanly.
No crashes, no hangs, no leaked windows after exit.

CC         = cc
COBC       = cobc
AR         = ar

SDL_CFLAGS = $(shell sdl2-config --cflags)
SDL_LIBS   = $(shell sdl2-config --libs)
COB_FLAGS  = -x -free -fstatic-call

.PHONY: all clean run run-imgtest

all: demo bounce imgtest

# ── framework static library ──────────────────────────────
pygame_cobol.o: pygame_cobol.c
	$(CC) -c -Wall -O2 $(SDL_CFLAGS) -o $@ $<

libpygame_cobol.a: pygame_cobol.o
	$(AR) rcs $@ $<

# ── test image ────────────────────────────────────────────
gen_test_bmp: gen_test_bmp.c
	$(CC) -Wall -O2 -o $@ $<

test.bmp: gen_test_bmp
	./gen_test_bmp

# ── COBOL programs ────────────────────────────────────────
demo: demo.cob libpygame_cobol.a pygame_cobol.cpy
	$(COBC) $(COB_FLAGS) demo.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(SDL_LIBS)

bounce: bounce.cob libpygame_cobol.a pygame_cobol.cpy
	$(COBC) $(COB_FLAGS) bounce.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(SDL_LIBS)

imgtest: imgtest.cob libpygame_cobol.a pygame_cobol.cpy test.bmp
	$(COBC) $(COB_FLAGS) imgtest.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(SDL_LIBS)

run: bounce
	./bounce

run-imgtest: imgtest
	./imgtest

clean:
	rm -f *.o *.a demo bounce imgtest gen_test_bmp test.bmp

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. FLAPPY-BIRD.

       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

      *> ── game loop control ──────────────────────────────────
       01 WS-RUNNING           BINARY-LONG VALUE 1.
       01 WS-HAS-EVENT         BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-TITLE             PIC X(80).
       01 WS-FLAP-REQ          BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.

      *> ── state: 0=waiting 1=playing 2=dead ─────────────────
       01 WS-STATE             BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-SCORE             BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.
       01 WS-SCORE-STR         PIC Z(2)9.

      *> ── layout constants ───────────────────────────────────
       78 WIN-W                VALUE 480.
       78 WIN-H                VALUE 640.
       78 GROUND-Y             VALUE 580.

      *> ── bird ───────────────────────────────────────────────
       78 BIRD-X               VALUE 80.
       78 BIRD-W               VALUE 30.
       78 BIRD-H               VALUE 22.
       78 BIRD-INIT-Y          VALUE 240.
       78 FLAP-VY              VALUE -9.
       78 VY-MAX               VALUE 12.
       01 WS-BIRD-Y            BINARY-LONG VALUE 240.
       01 WS-BIRD-VY           BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.

      *> ── pipe constants ─────────────────────────────────────
       78 PIPE-W               VALUE 52.
       78 GAP-H                VALUE 130.
       78 PIPE-SPD             VALUE 3.
       78 GAP-MIN              VALUE 60.
       78 GAP-RANGE            VALUE 320.
       78 PIPE-DIST            VALUE 200.

      *> ── pipe state (3 pipes) ───────────────────────────────
       01 WS-PIPES.
          05 WS-PIPE OCCURS 3.
             10 WS-PIPE-X      BINARY-LONG.
             10 WS-GAP-Y       BINARY-LONG.
             10 WS-SCORED       BINARY-LONG.

      *> ── PRNG seed ──────────────────────────────────────────
       01 WS-SEED              BINARY-LONG VALUE 0.

      *> ── timing ─────────────────────────────────────────────
       01 WS-T0                BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-T1                BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-DT                BINARY-LONG.

      *> ── scratch ────────────────────────────────────────────
       01 WS-I                 BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-TMP               BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-TMP2              BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-BOT-Y             BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-BOT-H             BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-B-BOT             BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-B-RT              BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-P-RT              BINARY-LONG.
       01 WS-CAP-X             BINARY-LONG.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PROGRAM.
           PERFORM INIT-SDL
           PERFORM RESET-GAME
           DISPLAY "Flappy COBOL ready"
           PERFORM GAME-LOOP UNTIL WS-RUNNING = 0
           CALL "pg_quit"
           STOP RUN.

       INIT-SDL.
           CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: pg_init failed"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF
           MOVE "Flappy COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
           CALL "pg_open_window" USING
               BY VALUE 480 BY VALUE 640
               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: pg_open_window failed"
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.

       RESET-GAME.
           MOVE BIRD-INIT-Y TO WS-BIRD-Y
           MOVE 0 TO WS-BIRD-VY
           MOVE 0 TO WS-SCORE
           MOVE 0 TO WS-STATE
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-SEED
           PERFORM VARYING WS-I FROM 1 BY 1
               UNTIL WS-I > 3
               COMPUTE WS-PIPE-X(WS-I) =
                   480 + (WS-I - 1) * 200
               PERFORM RAND-GAP
               MOVE 0 TO WS-SCORED(WS-I)
           END-PERFORM.

       RAND-GAP.
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-TMP
           ADD WS-SEED TO WS-TMP
           ADD 7919 TO WS-SEED
           IF WS-TMP < 0
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-TMP
           END-IF
           COMPUTE WS-TMP2 = WS-TMP / GAP-RANGE
           COMPUTE WS-GAP-Y(WS-I) =
               GAP-MIN + WS-TMP - WS-TMP2 * GAP-RANGE.

      *> ── main loop body ─────────────────────────────────────
       GAME-LOOP.
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-T0
           PERFORM HANDLE-INPUT
           IF WS-STATE = 1
               PERFORM UPDATE-WORLD
           END-IF
           PERFORM RENDER-FRAME
           PERFORM SET-TITLE
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-T1
           COMPUTE WS-DT = WS-T1 - WS-T0
           IF WS-DT < 16
               COMPUTE WS-TMP = 16 - WS-DT
               CALL "pg_delay" USING BY VALUE WS-TMP
           END-IF.

      *> ── input ──────────────────────────────────────────────
       HANDLE-INPUT.
           MOVE 0 TO WS-FLAP-REQ
           CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
               RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-HAS-EVENT = 0
               EVALUATE PG-EVT-TYPE
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-QUIT
                       MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN
                       IF PG-EVT-KEY = PG-KEY-ESCAPE
                           MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                       END-IF
                       IF PG-EVT-KEY = PG-KEY-SPACE
                          OR PG-KEY-UP
                           MOVE 1 TO WS-FLAP-REQ
                       END-IF
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN
                       IF PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN = PG-MOUSE-LEFT
                           MOVE 1 TO WS-FLAP-REQ
                       END-IF
               END-EVALUATE
               CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
                   RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           END-PERFORM
           IF WS-FLAP-REQ = 1
               EVALUATE WS-STATE
                   WHEN 0
                       MOVE 1 TO WS-STATE
                       MOVE FLAP-VY TO WS-BIRD-VY
                   WHEN 1
                       MOVE FLAP-VY TO WS-BIRD-VY
                   WHEN 2
                       PERFORM RESET-GAME
               END-EVALUATE
           END-IF.

      *> ── physics + pipes + collisions ───────────────────────
       UPDATE-WORLD.
           ADD 1 TO WS-BIRD-VY
           IF WS-BIRD-VY > VY-MAX
               MOVE VY-MAX TO WS-BIRD-VY
           END-IF
           ADD WS-BIRD-VY TO WS-BIRD-Y
           IF WS-BIRD-Y < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-BIRD-Y
               MOVE 0 TO WS-BIRD-VY
           END-IF

           PERFORM VARYING WS-I FROM 1 BY 1
               UNTIL WS-I > 3
               SUBTRACT PIPE-SPD FROM WS-PIPE-X(WS-I)
      *>       wrap when fully off left edge
               COMPUTE WS-TMP = WS-PIPE-X(WS-I) + PIPE-W
               IF WS-TMP < 0
                   ADD 600 TO WS-PIPE-X(WS-I)
                   PERFORM RAND-GAP
                   MOVE 0 TO WS-SCORED(WS-I)
               END-IF
      *>       score when pipe passes bird
               IF WS-SCORED(WS-I) = 0
                   COMPUTE WS-P-RT =
                       WS-PIPE-X(WS-I) + PIPE-W
                   IF WS-P-RT < BIRD-X
                       ADD 1 TO WS-SCORE
                       MOVE 1 TO WS-SCORED(WS-I)
                   END-IF
               END-IF
           END-PERFORM

           PERFORM CHECK-COLLISION.

      *> ── collision detection ────────────────────────────────
       CHECK-COLLISION.
           COMPUTE WS-B-BOT = WS-BIRD-Y + BIRD-H
           IF WS-B-BOT >= GROUND-Y
               COMPUTE WS-BIRD-Y = GROUND-Y - BIRD-H
               MOVE 2 TO WS-STATE
           END-IF

               COMPUTE WS-B-RT = BIRD-X + BIRD-W
               COMPUTE WS-B-BOT = WS-BIRD-Y + BIRD-H
               PERFORM VARYING WS-I FROM 1 BY 1
                   UNTIL WS-I > 3 OR WS-STATE = 2
                   COMPUTE WS-P-RT =
                       WS-PIPE-X(WS-I) + PIPE-W
                   IF WS-B-RT > WS-PIPE-X(WS-I)
                      AND BIRD-X < WS-P-RT
                       IF WS-BIRD-Y < WS-GAP-Y(WS-I)
                           MOVE 2 TO WS-STATE
                       END-IF
                       COMPUTE WS-BOT-Y =
                           WS-GAP-Y(WS-I) + GAP-H
                       IF WS-B-BOT > WS-BOT-Y
                           MOVE 2 TO WS-STATE
                       END-IF
                   END-IF
               END-PERFORM
           END-IF.

           MOVE SPACES TO WS-TITLE

               WHEN 0
                   MOVE "Flappy COBOL - Press SPACE"
                       TO WS-TITLE

           END-EVALUATE

      *>   sky

               BY VALUE 135 BY VALUE 206 BY VALUE 235
               BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_clear"

      *>   pipes

               BY VALUE 222 BY VALUE 184 BY VALUE 135

           CALL "pg_fill_rect" USING
               BY VALUE 0 BY VALUE GROUND-Y
               BY VALUE WIN-W BY VALUE 60
      *>   grass strip

               BY VALUE 86 BY VALUE 176 BY VALUE 0
               BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_fill_rect" USING
               BY VALUE 0 BY VALUE GROUND-Y
               BY VALUE WIN-W BY VALUE 6

                   BY VALUE 255 BY VALUE 60 BY VALUE 60
                   BY VALUE 255
           ELSE

                   BY VALUE 255 BY VALUE 220 BY VALUE 0
                   BY VALUE 255
           END-IF
           CALL "pg_fill_rect" USING
               BY VALUE BIRD-X BY VALUE WS-BIRD-Y
               BY VALUE BIRD-W BY VALUE BIRD-H

           MOVE WS-IMG-H TO WS-DISP-H
           DISPLAY "Loaded test.bmp: "
                   FUNCTION TRIM(WS-DISP-W) "x"
                   FUNCTION TRIM(WS-DISP-H) " pixels"
           PERFORM GAME-LOOP UNTIL WS-RUNNING = 0
           CALL "pg_free_image" USING BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
           CALL "pg_quit"
           STOP RUN.

       INIT-GRAPHICS.
           CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot initialise graphics"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           MOVE "COBOL Image Test" TO WS-TITLE
           CALL "pg_open_window" USING
               BY VALUE 640
               BY VALUE 480
               BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE
               BY VALUE 80
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC NOT = 0
               DISPLAY "ERROR: Cannot open window"
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF.

       TEST-ERROR-HANDLING.
           DISPLAY "--- Testing error handling ---"
           MOVE "nonexistent.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING PG-RC
           IF PG-RC = -1
               DISPLAY "  Load correctly failed (rc=-1)"
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "  Error: " PG-ERROR-MSG
           ELSE
               DISPLAY "  BUG: load should have failed!"
           END-IF
           DISPLAY "--- Error handling OK ---".

       LOAD-TEST-IMAGE.
           MOVE "test.bmp" TO WS-PATH
           CALL "pg_load_image" USING
               BY REFERENCE WS-PATH
               BY VALUE 256
               RETURNING WS-IMG-HANDLE
           IF WS-IMG-HANDLE = -1
               CALL "pg_get_error" USING
                   BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG
                   BY VALUE 256
               DISPLAY "Cannot load test.bmp: " PG-ERROR-MSG
               CALL "pg_quit"
               STOP RUN
           END-IF

           CALL "pg_image_width" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               RETURNING WS-IMG-W
           CALL "pg_image_height" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               RETURNING WS-IMG-H.

       GAME-LOOP.
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-START
           PERFORM POLL-EVENTS
           PERFORM UPDATE-STATE
           PERFORM RENDER
           CALL "pg_get_ticks" RETURNING WS-FRAME-END
           COMPUTE WS-ELAPSED = WS-FRAME-END - WS-FRAME-START
           IF WS-ELAPSED < 16
               COMPUTE WS-SLEEP-MS = 16 - WS-ELAPSED
               CALL "pg_delay" USING BY VALUE WS-SLEEP-MS
           END-IF.

       POLL-EVENTS.
           CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
               RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           PERFORM UNTIL WS-HAS-EVENT = 0
               EVALUATE PG-EVT-TYPE
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-QUIT
                       MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                   WHEN PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN
                       IF PG-EVT-KEY = PG-KEY-ESCAPE
                           MOVE 0 TO WS-RUNNING
                       END-IF
               END-EVALUATE
               CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
                   RETURNING WS-HAS-EVENT
           END-PERFORM.

       UPDATE-STATE.
           ADD WS-VX TO WS-IMG-X
           ADD WS-VY TO WS-IMG-Y

      *>   bounce horizontally
           IF WS-IMG-X < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-IMG-X
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-IMG-X + WS-IMG-W
               IF WS-EDGE > 640
                   COMPUTE WS-IMG-X = 640 - WS-IMG-W
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VX
               END-IF
           END-IF

      *>   bounce vertically
           IF WS-IMG-Y < 0
               MOVE 0 TO WS-IMG-Y
               MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
           ELSE
               COMPUTE WS-EDGE = WS-IMG-Y + WS-IMG-H
               IF WS-EDGE > 480
                   COMPUTE WS-IMG-Y = 480 - WS-IMG-H
                   MULTIPLY -1 BY WS-VY
               END-IF
           END-IF.

       RENDER.
      *>   dark background
           CALL "pg_set_color" USING
               BY VALUE 30 BY VALUE 30 BY VALUE 50 BY VALUE 255
           CALL "pg_clear"

      *>   bouncing image at native size
           CALL "pg_draw_image" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-X
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-Y

      *>   scaled copy (2x) pinned in the top-left corner
           CALL "pg_draw_image_sized" USING
               BY VALUE WS-IMG-HANDLE
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 8
               BY VALUE 96
               BY VALUE 96

           CALL "pg_present".

content.text:
Everything builds cleanly from scratch — all existing targets plus flappy, zero warnings.

Here's what's implemented in `flappy.cob`:

**Game states:** waiting (press SPACE to start) → playing → game-over (press SPACE to retry)

**Mechanics:**
- 480x640 portrait window, ~60fps frame limiting
- Bird at fixed x=80, gravity pulls down 1px/frame, flap impulse -9px/frame, terminal velocity 12px/frame
- 3 pipes scrolling left at 3px/frame, spaced 200px apart, wrapping with randomized gap positions
- Gap height 130px, gap Y range 60–379
- Score increments when a pipe's right edge passes the bird; shown in the window title
- AABB collision vs top pipe, bottom pipe, and ground → game over
- Space/Up arrow/left-click to flap; Escape or window close to exit

**Visual details:**
- Sky blue background, brown ground with green grass strip
- Green pipe bodies with darker cap lips at the gap openings
- Yellow bird (red when dead) with orange outline, white eye, black pupil

Run it with `make run-flappy`.

content.content:
1	# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL
2	
3	A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
4	coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
5	glue required in the COBOL source.
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	| Tool | Tested version |
10	|------|----------------|
11	| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
12	| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
13	| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
14	| GNU Make | 3.81+ |
15	
16	**macOS (Homebrew):**
17	
18	```sh
19	brew install gnucobol sdl2
20	```
21	
22	**Debian / Ubuntu:**
23	
24	```sh
25	sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
26	```
27	
28	> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
29	> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.
30	
31	## Build & run
32	
33	```sh
34	make              # compiles the library, all examples, and test.bmp
35	make run          # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
36	make run-imgtest  # builds and launches the image-loading test
37	./demo            # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
38	./bounce          # animated bouncing box (no input required)
39	./imgtest         # image loading, error handling, and drawing
40	```
41	
42	`make clean` removes all build artefacts.
43	
44	### bounce (animated example)
45	
46	Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
47	~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
48	window's close button to exit cleanly.
49	
50	### imgtest (image loading test)
51	
52	On startup: deliberately tries to load a missing file and prints the
53	error to the terminal (verifies error detection).  Then loads the
54	shipped `test.bmp`, queries its dimensions, and bounces it around the
55	window at native size while also drawing a 2× scaled copy in the
56	top-left corner.
57	
58	### demo (interactive example)
59	
60	Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
61	left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.
62	
63	## Architecture
64	
65	```
66	┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
67	│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
68	│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
69	│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
70	└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
71	```
72	
73	The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
74	never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.
75	
76	## Files
77	
78	| File | Purpose |
79	|------|---------|
80	| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
81	| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
82	| `bounce.cob` | Animated bouncing-box example (free-format COBOL) |
83	| `demo.cob` | Interactive demo — keyboard & mouse (free-format COBOL) |
84	| `imgtest.cob` | Image loading & error-handling test (free-format COBOL) |
85	| `gen_test_bmp.c` | Generates `test.bmp` (48×48 24-bit BMP) at build time |
86	| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a`, generates `test.bmp`, links all examples |
87	
88	## API reference
89

103	
104	| C signature | Purpose |

106	| `int pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each).  Returns 0. |

124	   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)

141	| `int pg_image_width(int handle)` | Pixel width of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |

186	    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE

188	        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
189	        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
190	        RETURNING PG-RC
191	    ...
192	    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
193	        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
194	    ...
195	    CALL "pg_quit"

197	```

199	Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
200	trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.
201	
202	## GnuCOBOL static-call fix
203	
204	By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
205	runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
206	executable, the runtime will fail with:
207	
208	```

210	```

213	generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
214	Makefile already passes this flag:
215	
216	```makefile

221	the same way:
222	
223	```sh

229	* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
230	  One window per process is the expected use case.
231	* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
232	  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
233	* **All C functions return `int`** — GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits
234	  `extern int name()` (K&R style) for every external `CALL`.  If the
235	  actual C function returns `void`, the caller reads garbage from the
236	  return register, which is undefined behaviour.  On ARM64 this can
237	  silently corrupt GnuCOBOL's `RETURN-CODE` and break control flow.
238	* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.

241	  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.

247	  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

252	* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make              # compiles the library, all examples, and test.bmp
make run          # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
make run-imgtest  # builds and launches the image-loading test
./demo            # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
./bounce          # animated bouncing box (no input required)
./imgtest         # image loading, error handling, and drawing
```

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

### bounce (animated example)

Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
window's close button to exit cleanly.

### imgtest (image loading test)

On startup: deliberately tries to load a missing file and prints the
error to the terminal (verifies error detection).  Then loads the
shipped `test.bmp`, queries its dimensions, and bounces it around the
window at native size while also drawing a 2× scaled copy in the
top-left corner.

### demo (interactive example)

Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `bounce.cob` | Animated bouncing-box example (free-format COBOL) |
| `demo.cob` | Interactive demo — keyboard & mouse (free-format COBOL) |
| `imgtest.cob` | Image loading & error-handling test (free-format COBOL) |
| `gen_test_bmp.c` | Generates `test.bmp` (48×48 24-bit BMP) at build time |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a`, generates `test.bmp`, links all examples |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `int pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each).  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle.  Returns 0. |

### Input

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |

Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:

```cobol
01 PG-EVENT.
   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
```

Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.

### Images

Supports **BMP** files (SDL2's built-in loader — no extra dependency).
Handles are 1-based integers (BINARY-LONG); -1 means error.

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_load_image(path, path_len)` | Load a BMP file.  Returns a handle (≥ 1) or -1 on error. |
| `int pg_image_width(int handle)` | Pixel width of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `int pg_image_height(int handle)` | Pixel height of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `int pg_draw_image(int handle, int x, int y)` | Draw the image at (x, y) at its native size.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_draw_image_sized(int handle, int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw the image scaled to w × h.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_free_image(int handle)` | Release the texture.  Safe to call twice.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_get_error(char *buf, int buf_len)` | Copy the last error message into a COBOL buffer (space-padded).  Returns 0. |

Up to 64 images may be loaded simultaneously.

Example (COBOL):

```cobol
01 WS-PATH   PIC X(256).
01 WS-HANDLE BINARY-LONG.

MOVE "sprite.bmp" TO WS-PATH
CALL "pg_load_image" USING
    BY REFERENCE WS-PATH BY VALUE 256
    RETURNING WS-HANDLE
IF WS-HANDLE = -1
    CALL "pg_get_error" USING
        BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG BY VALUE 256
    DISPLAY "Load failed: " PG-ERROR-MSG
END-IF
```

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `int pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime.  Returns 0. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## GnuCOBOL static-call fix

By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
executable, the runtime will fail with:

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

The fix is the **`-fstatic-call`** compiler flag, which makes `cobc`
generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
Makefile already passes this flag:

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **All C functions return `int`** — GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits
  `extern int name()` (K&R style) for every external `CALL`.  If the
  actual C function returns `void`, the caller reads garbage from the
  return register, which is undefined behaviour.  On ARM64 this can
  silently corrupt GnuCOBOL's `RETURN-CODE` and break control flow.
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

157	CALL "pg_load_image" USING
158	    BY REFERENCE WS-PATH BY VALUE 256
159	    RETURNING WS-HANDLE
160	IF WS-HANDLE = -1

178	WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
179	COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".
180	
181	01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
182	01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.
183

185	    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
186	    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
187	    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
188	        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
189	        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
190	        RETURNING PG-RC
191	    ...
192	    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
193	        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
194	    ...
195	    CALL "pg_quit"
196	    STOP RUN.
197	```
198	
199	Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
200	trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.
201	
202	## GnuCOBOL static-call fix
203	
204	By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
205	runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
206	executable, the runtime will fail with:
207

210	```

213	generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
214	Makefile already passes this flag:
215	
216	```makefile
217	COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
218	```
219

221	the same way:
222	
223	```sh
224	cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
225	```
226

228	
229	* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
230	  One window per process is the expected use case.
231	* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
232	  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
233	* **All C functions return `int`** — GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits
234	  `extern int name()` (K&R style) for every external `CALL`.  If the
235	  actual C function returns `void`, the caller reads garbage from the
236	  return register, which is undefined behaviour.  On ARM64 this can
237	  silently corrupt GnuCOBOL's `RETURN-CODE` and break control flow.
238	* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
239	  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
240	* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
241	  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
242	* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
243	  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
244	  vsync does most of the throttling.
245	* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
246	  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
247	  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).
248	
249	## Limitations
250	
251	* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
252	* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
253	* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
254	  is untested.

# COBOL-Pygame: a pygame-style graphics framework for GnuCOBOL

A thin C/SDL2 library that lets GnuCOBOL programs open a window, draw
coloured primitives, and handle keyboard/mouse input — no handwritten C
glue required in the COBOL source.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Tested version |
|------|----------------|
| GnuCOBOL (`cobc`) | 3.2.0 |
| SDL2 (`sdl2-config`) | 2.32.x |
| C compiler (cc/gcc/clang) | Apple Clang 16 |
| GNU Make | 3.81+ |

**macOS (Homebrew):**

```sh
brew install gnucobol sdl2
```

**Debian / Ubuntu:**

```sh
sudo apt install gnucobol4 libsdl2-dev
```

> The framework currently targets **macOS** and **Linux**.
> Windows should work under MSYS2/MinGW with the same packages but is untested.

## Build & run

```sh
make              # compiles the library, all examples, and test.bmp
make run          # builds (if needed) and launches the bounce example
make run-imgtest  # builds and launches the image-loading test
./demo            # interactive demo — arrow keys / WASD / mouse
./bounce          # animated bouncing box (no input required)
./imgtest         # image loading, error handling, and drawing
```

`make clean` removes all build artefacts.

### bounce (animated example)

Opens a 640×480 window with a cyan rectangle bouncing off the edges at
~60 fps (measure-and-sleep timing).  Press **Escape** or click the
window's close button to exit cleanly.

### imgtest (image loading test)

On startup: deliberately tries to load a missing file and prints the
error to the terminal (verifies error detection).  Then loads the
shipped `test.bmp`, queries its dimensions, and bounces it around the
window at native size while also drawing a 2× scaled copy in the
top-left corner.

### demo (interactive example)

Opens an 800×600 window.  Arrow keys or WASD move a red rectangle;
left-click teleports it.  Escape or close button quits.

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────┐  CALL "pg_*"   ┌──────────────────┐   SDL2 API   ┌───────┐
│  COBOL prog │ ──────────────► │ libpygame_cobol.a│ ────────────►│ SDL2  │
│  (demo.cob) │  BY VALUE /    │  (pygame_cobol.c) │              │       │
│             │  BY REFERENCE  │  singleton state  │              └───────┘
└─────────────┘                └──────────────────┘
```

The C layer maintains a **singleton** window and renderer.  COBOL programs
never handle raw pointers — every call targets the single implicit context.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `pygame_cobol.c` | Framework implementation (C / SDL2) |
| `pygame_cobol.cpy` | COBOL copybook — event record, key codes, constants |
| `bounce.cob` | Animated bouncing-box example (free-format COBOL) |
| `demo.cob` | Interactive demo — keyboard & mouse (free-format COBOL) |
| `imgtest.cob` | Image loading & error-handling test (free-format COBOL) |
| `gen_test_bmp.c` | Generates `test.bmp` (48×48 24-bit BMP) at build time |
| `Makefile` | Builds `libpygame_cobol.a`, generates `test.bmp`, links all examples |

## API reference

All functions use the C name shown below.  In COBOL, call them with
`CALL "pg_xxx"`.  Integer arguments are passed **BY VALUE** (BINARY-LONG).
Strings are passed **BY REFERENCE** followed by their length **BY VALUE**.

### Lifecycle

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_init(void)` | Initialise SDL2.  Returns 0 on success. |
| `int pg_quit(void)` | Destroy window/renderer and shut down SDL2.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_open_window(int w, int h, const char *title, int title_len)` | Open a resizable window.  Returns 0 on success. |

### Drawing

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_set_color(int r, int g, int b, int a)` | Set the current RGBA draw colour (0–255 each).  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_clear(void)` | Clear the window to the current colour.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_present(void)` | Flip the back-buffer so drawing becomes visible.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_draw_line(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)` | Draw a line between two points.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_draw_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw an outlined rectangle.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_fill_rect(int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw a filled rectangle.  Returns 0. |

### Input

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_poll_event(pg_event_t *evt)` | Non-blocking poll.  Returns 1 if an event was filled, 0 if the queue is empty. |

Pass **PG-EVENT BY REFERENCE** from COBOL.  The copybook defines:

```cobol
01 PG-EVENT.
   05 PG-EVT-TYPE       BINARY-LONG.   *> event type constant
   05 PG-EVT-KEY        BINARY-LONG.   *> SDL keycode (key events)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-X    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse X (motion/button)
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-Y    BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse Y
   05 PG-EVT-MOUSE-BTN  BINARY-LONG.   *> mouse button id
```

Event types: `PG-EVENT-QUIT`, `PG-EVENT-KEYDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-KEYUP`,
`PG-EVENT-MOUSEMOTION`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEDOWN`, `PG-EVENT-MOUSEUP`.

### Images

Supports **BMP** files (SDL2's built-in loader — no extra dependency).
Handles are 1-based integers (BINARY-LONG); -1 means error.

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_load_image(path, path_len)` | Load a BMP file.  Returns a handle (≥ 1) or -1 on error. |
| `int pg_image_width(int handle)` | Pixel width of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `int pg_image_height(int handle)` | Pixel height of a loaded image (0 if invalid handle). |
| `int pg_draw_image(int handle, int x, int y)` | Draw the image at (x, y) at its native size.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_draw_image_sized(int handle, int x, int y, int w, int h)` | Draw the image scaled to w × h.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_free_image(int handle)` | Release the texture.  Safe to call twice.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_get_error(char *buf, int buf_len)` | Copy the last error message into a COBOL buffer (space-padded).  Returns 0. |

Up to 64 images may be loaded simultaneously.

Example (COBOL):

```cobol
01 WS-PATH   PIC X(256).
01 WS-HANDLE BINARY-LONG.

MOVE "sprite.bmp" TO WS-PATH
CALL "pg_load_image" USING
    BY REFERENCE WS-PATH BY VALUE 256
    RETURNING WS-HANDLE
IF WS-HANDLE = -1
    CALL "pg_get_error" USING
        BY REFERENCE PG-ERROR-MSG BY VALUE 256
    DISPLAY "Load failed: " PG-ERROR-MSG
END-IF
```

### Timing & misc

| C signature | Purpose |
|-------------|---------|
| `int pg_delay(int ms)` | Sleep for the given number of milliseconds.  Returns 0. |
| `int pg_get_ticks(void)` | Monotonic millisecond counter (wraps after ~24 days). |
| `int pg_set_title(const char *title, int title_len)` | Change the window title at runtime.  Returns 0. |

## COBOL calling convention

```cobol
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
COPY "pygame_cobol.cpy".

01 WS-TITLE   PIC X(80).
01 WS-HAS-EVT BINARY-LONG.

PROCEDURE DIVISION.
    CALL "pg_init" RETURNING PG-RC
    MOVE "Hello from COBOL" TO WS-TITLE
    CALL "pg_open_window" USING
        BY VALUE 640 BY VALUE 480
        BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
        RETURNING PG-RC
    ...
    CALL "pg_poll_event" USING BY REFERENCE PG-EVENT
        RETURNING WS-HAS-EVT
    ...
    CALL "pg_quit"
    STOP RUN.
```

Strings are COBOL `PIC X(n)` fields passed BY REFERENCE; the C side trims
trailing spaces automatically, so no null-termination is needed.

## GnuCOBOL static-call fix

By default GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` resolves symbols **dynamically** at
runtime via `dlsym`.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a` is linked into the
executable, the runtime will fail with:

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

The fix is the **`-fstatic-call`** compiler flag, which makes `cobc`
generate direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.  The
Makefile already passes this flag:

```makefile
COB_FLAGS = -x -free -fstatic-call
```

If you write your own COBOL program against the framework, compile it
the same way:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **`-fstatic-call`** — required so GnuCOBOL resolves `pg_*` symbols at
  link time rather than via `dlsym` at runtime (see above).
* **All C functions return `int`** — GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits
  `extern int name()` (K&R style) for every external `CALL`.  If the
  actual C function returns `void`, the caller reads garbage from the
  return register, which is undefined behaviour.  On ARM64 this can
  silently corrupt GnuCOBOL's `RETURN-CODE` and break control flow.
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment padding.
  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `cobc -free`.  Remove the `-free`
  flag and adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer is created with vsync to avoid
  tearing.  The measure-and-sleep loop in `bounce.cob` is a safety net;
  vsync does most of the throttling.
* **Key codes** — the copybook exposes SDL keycode values directly.
  Letter keys are their ASCII values (a = 97 … z = 122).
  Arrow and function keys use SDL's extended range (> 1 billion).

## Limitations

* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

```sh

```

```sh

```

## Known gotchas

These are specific to the GnuCOBOL + C static library path.  Each
entry lists the symptom so you can match what you see to the fix.

### 1. Missing `-fstatic-call` — runtime symbol lookup fails

**Symptom:**

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

**Cause:** GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` defaults to resolving symbols
dynamically via `dlsym` at runtime.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a`
is linked into the executable, the runtime won't find the symbol.

**Fix:** Always compile with **`-fstatic-call`**, which makes `cobc`
emit direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

### 2. C functions must return `int`, never `void`

**Symptom:** The program compiles and links but behaves erratically —
exits immediately, corrupts `RETURN-CODE`, or crashes intermittently.
No error message is printed.

**Cause:** GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits `extern int name()` (K&R
style) for **every** external `CALL`.  If the actual C function returns
`void`, the caller reads whatever garbage is in the return register.
On ARM64 this can silently corrupt GnuCOBOL's internal return-code
register and break control flow.

**Fix:** Every C function in the framework must be declared as
`int func(...)` and return 0 (or a meaningful status code).  This is
already the case in `pygame_cobol.c` — if you add your own C helper
functions, follow the same pattern.

### 3. `FUNCTION TRIM` inside PERFORMed paragraphs (GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 / ARM64)

**Symptom:** A `PERFORM paragraph-name UNTIL ...` loop that follows a
paragraph containing `FUNCTION TRIM` executes zero iterations — the
program exits immediately with no error.

**Cause:** On GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 (ARM64/macOS), `cob_intr_trim` corrupts
runtime state that the `PERFORM UNTIL` loop-entry check depends on.
The loop condition evaluates as already-met, so the body never runs.

**Fix:** Do not use `FUNCTION TRIM` (or any `cob_intr_*` intrinsic)
inside a paragraph that is invoked via `PERFORM`.  Instead, use
`FUNCTION TRIM` inline in the main program flow, or avoid it entirely.
In the framework examples, string formatting is done without `TRIM`
(using `STRING ... DELIMITED SIZE` or `PIC Z(n)9` for numbers).

### 4. Missing `-free` — fixed-format column rules apply

**Symptom:**

```
error: PROGRAM-ID: invalid word 'PROGRAM-ID.'
```

or statements silently ignored because they fall outside columns 8-72.

**Cause:** GnuCOBOL defaults to fixed-format source, where code must
live in columns 8-72 and column 7 marks comments/continuations.  The
example `.cob` files use free format.

**Fix:** Compile with **`-free`** (already in the Makefile's
`COB_FLAGS`).

### 5. `BINARY-LONG` is required for C `int` mapping

The copybook uses `BINARY-LONG` for all integer fields
(`PG-EVENT`, `PG-RC`).  This maps exactly to C's `int32_t` with
native byte order and no alignment padding.  Do not substitute
`PIC 9(n)` or `COMP-3` — those use different internal representations
and will produce garbled values when the C function writes raw 32-bit
integers into them.

### 6. String length must accompany string arguments

Every string parameter in the C API takes two arguments: the buffer
BY REFERENCE and its length BY VALUE.

```cobol
*> WRONG — missing length:
CALL "pg_set_title" USING BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE

*> RIGHT:
CALL "pg_set_title" USING BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
```

The length tells the C side how many bytes to scan when trimming
trailing spaces.  Without it, the function reads a garbage length from
the stack.

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **All C functions return `int`** — required by GnuCOBOL's
  `-fstatic-call` code generation (see gotcha #2).
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment
  padding.  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the
  same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `-free`.  Remove the flag and
  adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer uses vsync to avoid tearing.
  The measure-and-sleep loop in the examples is a safety net; vsync
  does most of the throttling.

## Limitations

* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.

```cobol
                   CALL "pg_delay" USING BY VALUE 16
               END-IF
           END-PERFORM

           CALL "pg_quit"
           STOP RUN.
```

Build it the same way as the other examples:

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call skeleton.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

## Known gotchas

These are specific to the GnuCOBOL + C static library path.  Each
entry lists the symptom so you can match what you see to the fix.

### 1. Missing `-fstatic-call` — runtime symbol lookup fails

**Symptom:**

```
libcob: error: module 'pg_init' not found
```

**Cause:** GnuCOBOL's `CALL "name"` defaults to resolving symbols
dynamically via `dlsym` at runtime.  Even though `libpygame_cobol.a`
is linked into the executable, the runtime won't find the symbol.

**Fix:** Always compile with **`-fstatic-call`**, which makes `cobc`
emit direct C function calls instead of dynamic lookups.

```sh
cobc -x -free -fstatic-call myprog.cob -L. -lpygame_cobol $(sdl2-config --libs)
```

### 2. C functions must return `int`, never `void`

**Symptom:** The program compiles and links but behaves erratically —
exits immediately, corrupts `RETURN-CODE`, or crashes intermittently.
No error message is printed.

**Cause:** GnuCOBOL's `-fstatic-call` emits `extern int name()` (K&R
style) for **every** external `CALL`.  If the actual C function returns
`void`, the caller reads whatever garbage is in the return register.
On ARM64 this can silently corrupt GnuCOBOL's internal return-code
register and break control flow.

**Fix:** Every C function in the framework must be declared as
`int func(...)` and return 0 (or a meaningful status code).  This is
already the case in `pygame_cobol.c` — if you add your own C helper
functions, follow the same pattern.

### 3. `FUNCTION TRIM` inside PERFORMed paragraphs (GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 / ARM64)

**Symptom:** A `PERFORM paragraph-name UNTIL ...` loop that follows a
paragraph containing `FUNCTION TRIM` executes zero iterations — the
program exits immediately with no error.

**Cause:** On GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 (ARM64/macOS), `cob_intr_trim` corrupts
runtime state that the `PERFORM UNTIL` loop-entry check depends on.
The loop condition evaluates as already-met, so the body never runs.

**Fix:** Do not use `FUNCTION TRIM` (or any `cob_intr_*` intrinsic)
inside a paragraph that is invoked via `PERFORM`.  Instead, use
`FUNCTION TRIM` inline in the main program flow, or avoid it entirely.
In the framework examples, string formatting is done without `TRIM`
(using `STRING ... DELIMITED SIZE` or `PIC Z(n)9` for numbers).

### 4. Missing `-free` — fixed-format column rules apply

**Symptom:**

```
error: PROGRAM-ID: invalid word 'PROGRAM-ID.'
```

or statements silently ignored because they fall outside columns 8-72.

**Cause:** GnuCOBOL defaults to fixed-format source, where code must
live in columns 8-72 and column 7 marks comments/continuations.  The
example `.cob` files use free format.

**Fix:** Compile with **`-free`** (already in the Makefile's
`COB_FLAGS`).

### 5. `BINARY-LONG` is required for C `int` mapping

The copybook uses `BINARY-LONG` for all integer fields
(`PG-EVENT`, `PG-RC`).  This maps exactly to C's `int32_t` with
native byte order and no alignment padding.  Do not substitute
`PIC 9(n)` or `COMP-3` — those use different internal representations
and will produce garbled values when the C function writes raw 32-bit
integers into them.

### 6. String length must accompany string arguments

Every string parameter in the C API takes two arguments: the buffer
BY REFERENCE and its length BY VALUE.

```cobol
*> WRONG — missing length:
CALL "pg_set_title" USING BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE

*> RIGHT:
CALL "pg_set_title" USING BY REFERENCE WS-TITLE BY VALUE 80
```

The length tells the C side how many bytes to scan when trimming
trailing spaces.  Without it, the function reads a garbage length from
the stack.

## Design decisions

* **Singleton context** — avoids passing opaque pointers through COBOL.
  One window per process is the expected use case.
* **All C functions return `int`** — required by GnuCOBOL's
  `-fstatic-call` code generation (see gotcha #2).
* **BINARY-LONG everywhere** — maps to C `int32_t` with no alignment
  padding.  `COMP-5` / native-byte-order, so no endian issues on the
  same machine.
* **Free-format COBOL** — compiled with `-free`.  Remove the flag and
  adjust columns if you prefer fixed format.
* **SDL2 PRESENTVSYNC** — the renderer uses vsync to avoid tearing.
  The measure-and-sleep loop in the examples is a safety net; vsync
  does most of the throttling.

## Limitations

* No text rendering or audio.  Image loading is BMP-only (SDL2 built-in).
* `pg_get_ticks` returns a signed 32-bit int — wraps after ~24.8 days.
* Tested on macOS (arm64).  Linux should work out of the box; Windows
  is untested.
